# T005.1 - Port token validation

## Changes

- Added a separate ASP.NET Core `TokenValidator` in `DescopeSampleApp.Core/TokenValidator.cs`, registered with a named `HttpClient`, configured JWKS URL and injectable clock in `Program.cs`.
- Extended the in-memory JWKS fixture and added `TokenValidatorTests.cs` for signed tokens, invalid signatures, expiration, missing or malformed expiration, key selection, malformed JWKS, fetch failures, and unsupported algorithms.
- No legacy source, project, or routes changed. The new validator is not yet exposed through an API; that is T006.1.

## Behavioral evidence and choice

The unchanged legacy `VerifyTokenExpiration` currently returns false for all three characterized claims through the same exception fallback (T001.1). Those results do not prove the intended expiration comparison. The new service verifies the RS256 signature against a matching JWKS key and checks `exp` before returning the original JSON payload; this intentionally does **not** reproduce the legacy parser defect. Legacy nonempty-token HTTP behavior could not be characterized without live JWKS, so equivalence is not claimed. A fixed, nonproduction RSA fixture key and rejecting HTTP handler keep tests offline.

## Validation

- Full solution build: `msbuild -restore -p:RestorePackagesConfig=true -p:Configuration=Release -m -nologo -v:minimal` - pass; existing legacy jQuery NU1902 and assembly binding warnings remain.
- Full solution test: `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` - pass, 40 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (23 net48 and 17 net10).
- Lint: none defined.

## Risks

New validation rejects expired and missing-expiration tokens even though legacy expiration checks currently fail closed. The original validator performs live JWKS fetching, so complete wire compatibility is unverified until the new controller is exercised offline. The configured default project ID follows the unchanged legacy default; deployments must set `DESCOPE_PROJECT_ID` appropriately.
